parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.part_stem: Electrons are accelerated through a potential difference of $15\text{kV}$. The electrons collide with a metal target and a spectrum of X-rays is produced.
parts.text: Explain why a continuous spectrum of energies of X-ray photons is produced.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the wavelength of the highest energy X-ray photon produced.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem:
A beam of X-rays has an initial intensity $I_{\text{o}}$. The beam is directed into some body tissue. After passing through a thickness $x$ of tissue the intensity is $I$. The graph in Fig. 11.1 shows the variation with $x$ of $\ln (I/I_{\text{o}})$.
{{figure:figure_11_1}}
parts.text: Determine the linear attenuation (absorption) coefficient $\mu$ for this beam of X-rays in the tissue.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the thickness of tissue that the X-ray beam must pass through so that the intensity of the beam is reduced to 5.0% of its initial value.
